titre_page: How to make a tower defense in Yop2D? | Yop2D guide
description: Make a tower defense game in Yop2D, with no code: draw the enemies' path, send waves, build towers that pick a target and shoot, and count credits and base lives with nodes.
h1: How to make a tower defense?
carte: Draw a path, send waves, build towers that shoot and defend your base.
etapes: In Assets, tool « Path »: place points, link them, choose the start.
blocs: In a tower defense, **enemies** walk along a **path** and you build **towers** that shoot them before they reach your **base**. Here the enemies follow a path you draw yourself, each tower picks the closest enemy and fires at it, and **credits** pay for new towers.
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **map**: the background of the game, 1920 x 1080 px, with a road drawn on it;
a few {{lang:obj_prefix_image}}s for the build spots (for example 120 x 120 px);

an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} for the **enemy** (for example 64 x 64 px), one for the **tower** (120 x 120 px), one for the **cannon** (90 x 34 px, pointing right) and one for the **bullet** (24 x 24 px);
two {{lang:obj_prefix_texte}} objects: **creditsText** and **lifeText**, at the top of the screen.

This guide is written for a **1920 x 1080 landscape** game. The example **Tower defense (cubes)** (Examples tab) contains ready-made images in the folder **Images/TD**: open it and copy the ones you like into your project. You can also draw your own, the guide works with any style. The scenes **Enemy** and **Tower** are copied into the game many times: see the guide [Ready-made objects (prefabs)](guide:prefabs).

In the left panel, open the **{{lang:panneau_ress_variables}}** section and create two variables, both with scope **{{lang:var_scope_globale}}** (all the scenes can use them) and type **{{lang:var_type_entier}}**:
**credits**: starting value **150** (the money to build towers);
**base_life**: starting value **20** (how many enemies your base can take).
The enemies follow a **path**: points linked together. You draw it on top of your map with the Path tool.
Open the **Assets** window (Resources panel) and touch **Path**. The path editor opens, with your scene in the background.

With the tool **Place points**, touch the scene to place a first point on the left, where the enemies come in: it is the **Start**. Keep touching along your road: each new point is linked to the previous one.
Put the last point on your base: it has no exit, it is the **End**.
Touch **Watch it go** to see a dot travel along the path. Then close the editor: the path is saved by itself.
To change the start, touch a point and choose **Make this point the start**. To move a point, use the tool **Move**; to remove one, use **Erase**.
An enemy is a **scene** of its own: every enemy you send into the game is a **copy** of it, with its own life. You build it once.
Create a new scene named **Enemy** (menu **＋**, then **{{lang:popup_creer_scene_titre}}**).
In the scene **Enemy**, add an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **enemy** at X = `0`, Y = `0`, and give it the tag **enemy**.
Open the **{{lang:titre_blueprint}}** of the scene **Enemy** and add the **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event.
Link the three nodes in order.
Now go back to your main scene (**Game**) and send enemies one after the other.
Open the **{{lang:titre_blueprint}}** of the scene **Game** and add the **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event.
Add two **[[modifier_variable]]** nodes: **credits** = `150`, then **base_life** = `20`. They start every new game clean, even after a Game Over.
Add **[[attendre]]**: **{{lang:attendre.duree}}** = `3` (a pause before the first enemy).
From the **{{lang:port_a_chaque_fois}}** output, add **[[placer_copie_scene]]**: scene **Enemy**. Leave X and Y as they are: the enemy goes to the start of the path by itself.
Run the game: an enemy appears every second and a half and walks along your path to the end (nothing happens when it arrives yet).
A tower is also a **scene**. It looks for the closest enemy in range, turns its cannon toward it and fires.
Create a new scene named **Tower**. Add an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} **tower** at X = `0`, Y = `0`, then an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} **cannon** at X = `15`, Y = `43`, in front of it.

In the scene **Game**, add an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **bullet** **outside the screen** (for example X = `-300`, Y = `-300`) and give it the tag **bullet**: it is the model the tower copies at each shot.

Open the **{{lang:titre_blueprint}}** of the scene **Tower** and add the **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event, then **[[repeter]]**: **{{lang:repeter.delai}}** = `0.2`, **{{lang:repeter.repetitions}}** = `0` (endless). The tower looks around 5 times per second.

From the **{{lang:port_a_chaque_fois}}** output, add **[[choisir_cible]]**: target **tower**, **{{lang:choisir_cible.tag}}** = `enemy`, **{{lang:choisir_cible.regle}}** = **[[lang:option.cb_proche]]**, and in the advanced settings **{{lang:choisir_cible.portee_px}}** = `330`.
From the **{{lang:port_trouvee}}** output, add **[[orienter_vers]]**: target **cannon**, and as the second object choose **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}** (the enemy that was chosen).
Add **[[cooldown]]**: target **cannon**, **{{lang:cooldown.delai}}** = `1.2` (one shot every 1.2 seconds at most).

From the **{{lang:port_pret}}** output, add **[[tirer]]**: target **cannon**, **{{lang:tirer.modele}}** = `bullet`, **{{lang:tirer.vitesse}}** = `14`, **{{lang:tirer.duree_vie}}** = `1.6`, **{{lang:tirer.detruire_hors_ecran}}** = no. Leave **{{lang:tirer.direction}}** as it is: the bullet leaves in the direction the cannon is facing.
Place a **Tower** by hand into the scene **Game** to test it (menu **＋** → the scene **Tower**): it should shoot at every enemy that passes within 330 pixels.
This part goes in the scene **Enemy**: it is the enemy that knows when a bullet touches it.
Open the **{{lang:titre_blueprint}}** of the scene **Enemy** and add the **[[NoeudEventCollisionTag]]** event: target **enemy**, {{lang:Tag}} **bullet**.
Add **[[detruire_objet]]** and choose **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}** as the target: it is the bullet, which disappears.
Add **[[infliger_degats]]**: target **enemy**, **{{lang:infliger_degats.degats}}** = `1`. By default the enemy is destroyed when its life reaches zero.
From the **{{lang:port_detruit}}** output, add **[[ajouter_variable]]**: variable **credits**, value `15` (the reward).
The player builds a tower by touching a **build spot**. It costs 50 credits.
Select each build spot and give it the tag **spot** in the Inspector.
In the scene **Game**, add the **[[NoeudEventClicObjet]]** event and choose **# spot** as the object (every object with the tag **spot**).

Then **[[placer_copie_scene]]**: scene **Tower**. For **X**, touch **🔗**, choose **[[valeur_objet]]**, object **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}**, **{{lang:valeur_objet.propriete}}** = `x`. Do the same for **Y** with `y`: the tower appears exactly where the player touched.
Add **[[detruire_objet]]** with **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}** as the target: the build spot disappears.
On the **{{lang:port_faux}}** output: **[[toast]]** with the message **Not enough credits**.
In the scene **Game**, add the **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]** event.
Link the three nodes in order.
Step 9: base lives and game over
When an enemy reaches the end of the path, your base loses a life. When the base has none left, the game is over.
In the scene **Enemy**, take the **[[suivre_parcours]]** node of step 3. From its **{{lang:port_arrive}}** output, add **[[ajouter_variable]]**: variable **base_life**, value `-1`.
Add **[[condition]]** `=base_life <= 0`. On the **{{lang:port_vrai}}** output, add **[[appeler_evenement]]** with the event name **game_over**.
In the scene **Game**, add the **[[NoeudEventPersonnalise]]** event with the same name **game_over**.
Add **[[arreter_minuteur]]**: **{{lang:arreter_minuteur.nom}}** = `waves` (no more enemies are sent), then **[[detruire_par_tag]]**: **{{lang:detruire_par_tag.tag}}** = `enemy`.
Add **[[toast]]** with the message **Game over**, then **[[attendre]]** `2` seconds, then **[[recommencer_scene]]**.
Play: build a tower or two with your credits, then watch them stop the enemies. Let a few get through to see the base lose its lives.
**Victory:** count the enemies with a variable (+1 when one dies or arrives). When the number reaches the total you sent, show a message and win.

**Upgrade a tower:** touch a tower to open a small window with a button « Upgrade » that costs credits and changes the cannon image and the speed of fire. Open the example **Tower defense (cubes)** to see how.
**Several enemy types:** make a second scene (**Enemy2**) with more life and another speed, and let each wave send one or the other (open the example **Tower defense (cubes)** to see how).
**Crossroads:** in the Path tool, touch a point and choose **This point is a crossroads**: the enemies pick a road at random, and the branches can join again.

**Several lanes and no traffic jams:** in **[[suivre_parcours]]**, set **{{lang:suivre_parcours.ecart}}** and **{{lang:suivre_parcours.eviter}}** to yes: the enemies walk side by side and overtake each other.
**A big map:** make your map twice as wide, then add **[[limites_camera]]** and **[[camera_doigt]]** at the start so the player scrolls the map with a finger.
**Sounds and sparks:** add **[[jouer_son]]** at each shot and an **[[effet_particules]]** when an enemy dies (see the guide [Particles and effects](guide:particules-effets)).

**The enemies don't move:** check that the **{{lang:suivre_parcours.parcours}}** setting is the name of your path (**Path**), and that the path has a Start. Check that the scene **Enemy** has its **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event.

**The tower doesn't shoot:** check the tag **enemy** on the enemy, the name **bullet** in **[[tirer]]**, and that the **bullet** object is in the scene **Game** (outside the screen, but not deleted). Raise **{{lang:choisir_cible.portee_px}}** if the enemies stay out of range.
**The bullets don't hurt:** the bullet must have the tag **bullet**, and the event **[[NoeudEventCollisionTag]]** must be in the scene **Enemy**, not in **Game**.
**The tower appears in the wrong place:** for **X** and **Y** of **[[placer_copie_scene]]**, use the green **[[valeur_objet]]** nodes with **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}**, as in step 7.
**The credits or the base lives don't change:** check that the variables **credits** and **base_life** have the scope **{{lang:var_scope_globale}}**.
